hypotheses.claim: Replacing a plain multiplicative gate product with a stagnation-adaptive rank-power exponent p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) that decays monotonically (≈2.0 greedy worst-removal -> ≈0.7 quasi-random diversification) will reduce mean objective on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 below the current SBS 15.9986, with the largest per-instance gains concentrated in the known weakest regimes (capacity_level=tight, size=100, demand_dist=uniform, depot_style=eccentric, spatial=clustered); the effect is attributed to escaping LNS stagnation within the 500 ms unified deadline rather than to extra iterations.

next_search_advice.direction: Stagnation-adaptive multiplicative gating + regime-targeted diversification in score_ruin_nodes: normalize removal savings by a global depot-distance scale, then multiply by (i) a capacity-pressure gate that raises priority for nodes on near-full routes (targets weak regime capacity_level=tight), (ii) a depot-distance-balance gate that alternates between near-depot and far-depot nodes as iter_frac grows (targets weak regime depot_style=eccentric), (iii) a route-local-density gate that prefers nodes whose route neighbors are far (clustered spatial), and (iv) apply rank_power with exponent p that decreases from ~2.0 to ~0.7 as stagnation_ratio rises, so the policy is greedy-worst early and becomes diversification/random-ish when stuck. Preserve determinism (no RNG; ties broken by node index).
